title: Serpens Nebula (NIRCam image)
caption: The Serpens Nebula, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: Serpens Nebula · constellation Serpens Cauda · about 1300 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, K. Pontoppidan (NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory), J. Green (Space Telescope Science Institute)

recognition.text: Ranked #68 on ESA/Webb’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Layers of wispy gas and dust in orange, red and blue fill this young stellar nursery. In the upper left, amid mostly orange dust, several small red plumes all point the same way, and at the center a bright star sits within an hourglass-shaped shadow. This is the Serpens Nebula, 1 300 light-years from Earth, in a view from Webb's Near-InfraRed Camera.
Those red streaks are the key finding. They are shockwaves where jets from young stars slam into surrounding gas, and they form a group of aligned outflows in one small corner of the nebula.

The Serpens Nebula holds an especially crowded cluster of stars still forming, around 100 000 years old, and some will eventually grow to the mass of the Sun. The hourglass at the center is the flapping Bat Shadow, named after Hubble data from 2020 revealed it shifting.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (6.59 x 4.17 arcminutes) and distance (1300 light years), the frame spans roughly 2.5 × 1.6 light-years. Its light set out about 1,300 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This near-infrared image from Webb's NIRCam shows a 1.4-micron filter in blue, a 2.1-micron filter in cyan, a 3.6-micron filter in orange and a 4.8-micron filter in red.
understand.eye: This light is infrared and invisible to the eye, and some of the densest dust here blocks even infrared light.

explore: To the right of the Bat Shadow is an eye-shaped crevice that looks as if a star is bursting through. Astronomers caution it may simply be gas of different densities layered on top of each other, as in the Pillars of Creation. Farther right, a very dark patch may be dust so dense that no near-infrared light gets through.
The black rectangles at two corners mark missing data.
alt: Wispy orange, red and blue gas and dust, with small red plumes at upper left, a bright central star with an hourglass shadow, an eye-shaped crevice to its right, and black rectangles of missing data at two corners.
